Nitrogen form N2 (i.e. N≡N ) but phosphorus form P4 , because in P2 , pπ−pπ bonding is present which is a weaker bonding.

Nitrogen is smaller in size hence it forms multiple bond with other nitrogen atom ( N≡N )

However heavier elements of this group do not form pπ−pπ bonds as their atomic orbitals are so large and diffuse that they cannot have effective overlapping. Thus nitrogen exist as diatomic molecule with a triple bonds.

The single P - P bond is stronger and has higher catenation tendency

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following statements are true.

(i) In the structure of   HNO 3,  the   N−O  bond (121 pm) is shorter than the   N−OH  bond (140 pm).

(ii) All the   P−Cl  bonds in   PCl 5  are not equivalent.

(iii)   I−Cl  is more reactive than   I 2 .
questions.solution:
(i) N−O bond is shorter than N−OH bond in HNO 3 molecule. It can be understood with the help of resonating structures of HNO 3 molecule.

As we can see from the resonating structures, there is double bond character between N−O bonds but there is always single bond character between N−OH bond. This is because of no pi-bonding occurring between nitrogen and oxygen of −OH group.

Double bond is shorter than single bond. So N−O bond is shorter than N−OH bond in HNO 3 molecule.

(ii) There are two bonds in PCl 5 . One is equatorial and other is axial, because of the repulsion factor one is longer and the other shorter.

(iii) I−Cl bond is weaker than I−I bond
